title: Control of Cell Adhesion using Hydrogel Patterning Techniques for Applications in Traction Force Microscopy
protocol: Prepare a 300 mL solution by adding 10 mL of double distilled water into a clean 400 mL glass beaker placed inside a fume hood.
Add 18.75 mL of acetic acid to the beaker using a serological pipette.
Add 18.75 mL of 3-(Trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate to the solution in the beaker.
Add 252.5 mL of ethanol to the mixture.
Pour the prepared solution into a crystallizing dish.
Clean 24 mm round glass coverslips with precision wipes.
Place cleaned coverslips in a custom-made polytetrafluorethylene rack.
Immerse the rack containing coverslips into the methacrylation solution and incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse all coverslips with ethanol after removing them from the solution.
Dry the coverslips under air flow.
Take a 15 mm round glass coverslip and place it on a Petri dish.
Mark the upper side of the coverslip using a diamond pen.
Clean the coverslip via oxygen plasma treatment at 0.4 mbar and 200 W for 2 min.
Pipette 100 µL of 0.01% poly-L-lysine solution on the surface of each coverslip.
Incubate the coverslips for 30 min at room temperature (RT).
Wash the coverslips with 10 mM HEPES pH 8.5.
Remove excess liquid but keep the surface wet.
Pipette 100 µL of 50 mg/mL mPEG-SVA in 10 mM HEPES pH 8.5 on the surface of each coverslip.
Incubate the coverslips for 1 h at RT.
Rinse the coverslips with 10 mM HEPES pH 8.5 and dry off under air flow.
Add 2 µL of UV-sensitive photoinitiator (e.g., PLPP-gel) followed by 40 µL of ethanol onto the surface.
Gently tilt the Petri dish back and forth to obtain a homogeneous distribution of the gel and ethanol on the surface.
Wait for 5 min for the solution to polymerize.
Place a single coverslip inside a 35 mm Petri dish with a 20 mm hole at the bottom.
Turn on the microscope.
Calibrate the UV-A laser on the 20x air objective.
Place the sample with the photoinitiator on the stage.
Adjust the focus on the surface of the glass.
Turn on the focus control.
Load and lock the pre-drawn pattern.
Prepare the pattern using a graphics software like Inkscape.
Ensure that the pattern file does not exceed the DMD dimensions (1824 x 1140 px, which corresponds to 552 x 325 µm on 20x lens).
Use the DMD size as the pattern file size for accurate patterning.
For pattern transfer to polyacrylamide, ensure patterning is done only up to 60%-70% of the radius from the center of the glass to the edge.
For a single cell, use a diameter of 50-100 µm with a distance of 100 µm between patterns and a diameter of 150-300 µm for a cell group.
Start the patterning by UV dose of 30 mJ/mm².
The patterning duration depends on the number of patterns, making one pattern take approximately 1 second.
Rinse the surface with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) three times.
Incubate the sample with 100 µL of 25 µg/mL fibronectin dissolved in 1x PBS and 25 µg/mL fibrinogen Alexa488 conjugate in PBS for 1 h at RT.
Rinse the surface with 1x PBS three times.
Put methacrylated glass coverslips into a Petri dish.
Add 9.55 mL of double-distilled water into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 0.5 mL of HEA to the centrifuge tube.
Add 42 mg of sodium(meta)periodate to the centrifuge tube.
Stir the solution continuously in the dark for 4 h.
Mix acrylamide, bis-acrylamide, and double-distilled water according to Table 1 to prepare 10 mL of stock solution hydrogel.
Degas the stock solution and close the lid to an airtight seal.
Keep the stock solution in aliquots for up to 1 year at 4 °C.
Characterize the Young's modulus of the hydrogel prior to use.
Start with the bottom layer by gently mixing 99.3 µL of stock solution, 0.5 µL of 1% ammonium persulfate (APS), and 0.2 µL of tetramethylethylenediamine (TEMED) in a 1.5 mL tube.
Pipette 10 µL from the bottom layer solution dropwise on the center of the methacrylated coverslip.
Carefully place a 15 mm round coverslip on the droplet and wait for 45 min for polymerization.
Gently detach the top coverslip with a scalpel.

For the top layer, gently mix 93.3 µL of stock solution with 1 µL of fresh oxidized HEA solution, 5 µL of fluorescent beads (corresponding to three beads per square micron for beads of 200 nm sized beads), 0.5 µL of 1% APS, and 0.2 µL of TEMED in a 1.5 mL tube.
Pipette 5 µL from the top layer solution dropwise on the center of the already polymerized bottom layer.
Gently place the micropatterned coverslip on the droplet.
Wait for 45 min at RT for the droplet to polymerize, ensuring the patterned side touches the droplet.
Gently detach the coverslip with a scalpel.
Glue the 24 mm coverslips to the bottom of custom-drilled 6-well plates using two-component silicone-glue.
Add PBS to the wells after 5 minutes.
Mount a spherical tip cantilever on the AFM holder.
Calibrate each cantilever by acquiring a force-distance curve on a hard substrate.
Extrapolate the cantilever sensitivity from the acquired curve.
Retract from the surface and perform a thermal tune to get their spring constant.
Place calibrated cantilevers over the hydrogel sample.
Acquire force curves in PBS buffer using specified parameters.
Plot the acquired force versus distance curves with AFM analysis software.
Find the contact point on the plotted curves.
Convert force versus distance curves into force versus indentation curves.
Fit the indentation part of the curve with Hertz model or a suitable mechanics model based on tip geometry.
Aspirate PBS from the wells.
Seed 3 x 10^6 cells per 6-well plate in growth medium.
Incubate cells overnight at 37 °C/5% CO2.
Wash samples to remove floating cells before starting microscopy.
Turn on the microscope incubation chamber and gas supply to obtain a temperature of 37 °C and 5% CO2 atmosphere.
Turn on the microscope and the laser patterning module.
Place the custom-made 6-well plate with the samples on the stage.
Adjust focus on the surface of the PA.
Setup the illumination pattern and mark the cells of interest.
Refocus on the surface of the hydrogel.
Acquire the image of the cells in the brightfield channel.
Switch to the Cy5 channel and take an image of beads in the deformed state.
Shift to the laser channel.
Turn on the laser for 3 min at a dose of 6,000 mJ/mm².
Switch to the Cy5 channel and acquire an image of the beads in the undeformed state.
For mouse embryonic fibroblasts, wait for 15 min post-exposure to record the reference/undeformed image.
Repeat steps 4.5-4.7 again for another cell(s) of interest.
To measure elevated oxidative stress after UV-A illumination, add 5 µM CellRox into the imaging media and incubate for 30 min at 37 °C/5% CO2.
Wash the cells 3x with warm 1x PBS.
Replace the imaging media.
Record the Cy5 signal by fluorescence imaging before and after UV-A illumination.
Open fluorescent beads images before and after laser treatment using Fiji.
Merge two images as one stack.
Correct lateral drift between the two images using StackReg plugin.
Change images to 8 bit.
Resize images to 1024 x 1024 pixels.
Save the merged image sequence in TIFF format with the reference image at the beginning.
Acquire the displacement vector field using a cross-correlation technique from the PIV-field as implemented in the OpenPIV project.
Choose search window sizes wR and wD of 32 pixels each for relaxed (undeformed) and deformed images, respectively.
Ensure an overlap of 70% between neighboring search windows.
Determine a displacement vector for each search window that optimizes the cross-correlation function.
Assign the determined displacement vector to the center position of the search window.
Obtain subpixel accuracy using a Gaussian fit around the maxima region.
Find and remove ambiguous displacement vectors.
Discard displacement vectors where the ratio between two highest local maxima is below 1.5.
Remove displacement vectors that fail the normalized median test for a residual threshold of 1.5.
(Optional) Correct lateral drift by subtracting a fixed vector from all displacements.
Interpolate the resulting displacement vector field to a regular grid with spacing of 4 px using cubic polynomial interpolation.
Fill missing datapoints using a smooth bivariate spline extrapolation.
Relate a displacement vector in pixels to local deformation by the pixel ratio (0.33 µm/px for 20x air lens).
(Optional) Mirror pad the image to reduce ringing artifacts in subsequent analysis.
Multiply the deformation field by a Tukey window function with parameters 0.2-0.3.
Reconstruct the traction using regularized Fourier Transform Traction Cytometry (FTTC).
Use 0th order Tikhonov regularization for the reconstruction.
Choose an optimal regularization parameter λ that minimizes the Generalized Cross Validation (GCV) function.
Apply a Lanzcos filter to reduce artifacts due to limited frequency space and displacement field upsampling.
